notes: Puts the published legal documents inside the three apps, sliced per role. The founder asked for exactly this: 'some we add to brand app, some to influencer and some to follower. we dont keep all in all apps.' Result — Brand 12, Creator 10, Follower 8, web 14. The rule applied throughout: a person sees the documents that BIND THEM; showing a shopper the Creator Agreement does not make INFLX more transparent, it buries the refund policy they opened the screen to find. Two judgement calls worth knowing: Advertising Disclosure is in the BRAND app too (a brand is responsible for its creators labelling paid posts, not just the creator), and Refunds is in the brand app (brands must honour them). Cookie Policy is web-only — cookies are a browser concern, app tracking is covered by the Privacy Policy, and it would waste a slot in three mobile menus; every app links out to inflx.in/legal so nothing is unreachable, just not in the way. ARCHITECTURE FORCED BY METRO: Metro cannot resolve outside Packages/Mobile/, the same constraint that makes src/components/InflxMark.js a deliberate duplicate and is documented in src/utils/tracking.js. So rather than hand-maintain a second copy of ~90KB of legal text, scripts/sync-legal-to-mobile.mjs GENERATES src/legal/content.js from brand-web with company tokens resolved at build time. A generated file that can quietly go stale is worse than no generated file — the website would show a corrected policy while three apps served the old text — so the script has a --check mode that re-renders in memory and fails, and qa/unit/legal-sync.spec.ts runs it inside pnpm qa. CRASH-CLASS CARE: a duplicate Stack.Screen name in native-stack is a hard crash on tab mount (logged in auto-memory from a previous incident). Each of LegalList and LegalDocument is registered exactly ONCE per navigator, verified by grep; the follower ProfileStack deliberately does not spread SHARED_SCREENS so there is no hidden second registration to collide with. Tables render as STACKED CARDS rather than scrolling sideways, because a real table at 300px squeezes text into a column two words wide and a legal document that is annoying to read does not get read. The screens make no network call, so Legal works signed-out and offline. ANTI-FAKE-GREEN: the role-leak guard was MUTATION-CHECKED — adding 'shopper' to the Creator Agreement's audiences and resyncing made the shopper set 9 documents and failed TWO tests (the leak assertion and the list-screen assertion that a shopper never sees that title); reverted, checksum back to 25df7605b92f285f confirmed by --check. One test was corrected rather than the code, and it was strengthened in the process: the document-render assertion used an exact-string match on a section heading, but a heading renders as two nested Text nodes so the parent's text content is number + heading and an exact match cannot see it — replaced with a contained-match AND extended to assert the first paragraph rendered, so it now proves the body appeared rather than just the chrome. UPSTREAM CORRECTION CARRIED IN: before the web publish, every claim in the documents was checked against the actual app rather than assumed. cancelOrder EXISTS in the follower app so that instruction stands; Return/report-a-problem, ticket numbers and in-app Delete Account DO NOT exist, and the wording was softened to email/phone/web routes. The deletion page had been telling users to open Profile > Settings > Delete account, a menu that is not there — which matters because Play Store checks that exact route. VERIFIED: Mobile jest 27 suites / 131 tests green (13 new); pnpm qa GREEN 125/125 gate 0 (was 124, +1 for the sync workflow); generator reports brand: 12 / creator: 10 / shopper: 8; grep confirms one registration per navigator per route. NOT VERIFIED: no on-device run — adb devices was empty so Maestro did not run, and released stays false per Rule 5; the agency flavour has no Legal entry (out of scope, recorded). PRODUCTION-IMPACTING VIA OTA ONLY — JS-only, no native change, so no APK rebuild is needed. No backend, no migration, no Vercel deploy.
